confirm.stopDesc: Deletes the CR, Pods, ALB and SageMaker endpoint to release compute. The config and logs are kept, so you can clone it to rebuild the service.
confirm.deleteDescList: This also deletes the IEC CR, Pods and ALB.
confirm.deleteDescDetail: This also deletes the IEC CR, Pods and ALB.

messages.stopped: Inference service stopped (the config and logs are kept; clone it to rebuild)

list.description: Inference services based on the HyperPod InferenceEndpointConfig (SGLang engine). Models are loaded from FSx or S3, and the API is OpenAI-compatible.
list.filterHint: Filtering is limited to the latest 5000 items.

tips.status: The inference service's own runtime status (CR phase). DeploymentComplete: running; DeploymentInProgress: deploying; DeploymentFailed: failed; Stopped: stopped; Deleted: deleted. Click the magnifier for the full status details.
tips.queueStatus: The inference service's status in the Kueue scheduling queue (separate from its own status). Queued: waiting for quota; Admitted: admitted by Kueue; Evicted: evicted from the queue; and so on.
tips.framework: Inference engine: SGLang (high throughput, the primary choice) / vLLM / TRT-LLM. The framework determines the set of launch arguments and the optimizations available (such as KV cache and quantization schemes).
tips.spec: Resources requested by the inference service: number of replicas × GPUs per replica. Hover over the tag to see the instance type. With multiple replicas, an ALB balances the load.

statusTip.phaseSource: InferenceEndpointConfig CR.status.deploymentStatus.deploymentObjectOverallState (falls back to status.state if missing)

pending.detail: The CR has been created, but the IEC Operator has not started processing it yet (queued for reconcile).

deploying.detail: The Operator is creating the Deployment, pulling the model weights (FSx / S3 / HuggingFace Hub), starting the SGLang or vLLM engine, and configuring the ALB target group. This is the most common "waiting to load" state.

running.detail: Target terminal state: the Pod is Ready, the ALB health check passes, and the SageMaker endpoint is InService, so the service can take OpenAI-compatible traffic from outside. With multiple replicas, an ALB balances the load.

failed.label: Deployment failed
failed.detail: Terminal failure state: the model weights could not be pulled, SGLang ran out of memory on startup, there were not enough GPUs, the ALB target group health check failed, and so on. Check the Pod logs or the "Status timeline" card on the details page.

stopped.detail: Sentinel state (not a raw CR value; written by the backend stop API): the Pods, ALB and SageMaker endpoint are all destroyed to release compute. The CR record is still kept (in DDB) and the config and logs remain viewable, so you can rebuild the service with "Clone config".

For notes in other languages such as Chinese, use the "Description" field below. The final task name = this name + '-' + 10 random characters, generated by the backend at creation.

launch.heading: Launch script (SGLang)
launch.help:
The whole script runs via /bin/sh -c (the backend renders command=["/bin/sh","-c"], args=[script]).
Use exec to take over the main process. --model-path is required and must be the absolute model path (for FSx, the path you see in the dev instance, such as /fsx/checkpoint).
Edit --tp / --mem-fraction-static / --context-length and similar flags directly here.
launch.scriptExtra: A complete SGLang launch command is pre-filled; edit it as needed (the port must match the container port under Compute resources; avoid 8081, which is used by the platform's reverse proxy).
launch.metricsLabel: Enable metrics (SGLang /metrics + DCGM, connected to AMP automatically)
launch.metricsHint: If disabled, do not include --enable-metrics in the script.
launch.publicHint: Off by default: the service can only be invoked from inside the cluster or the VPC (ClusterIP / ALB). If on, an extra public SageMaker endpoint is created (invoked with boto3 or the CLI using SigV4), which uses 1 additional IP per subnet.
